players.product: fiber network carrier deploying Corning Gen AI fiber and cable systems for data center interconnects and fiber-to-the-home

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Stansbury), 'in line with our expectations and updated 2025 guidance': total reported revenue declined 8.7% to $3.041 billion; Business segment revenue declined 8.8% to $2.425 billion (including 'over three fifty basis points' of anticipated downward impact from one-time dark fiber and elevated public sector harvest revenue in 2024); Mass Markets revenue declined 7.9% to $616 million; adjusted EBITDA $767 million (25.2% margin) versus approximately $1.052 billion a year ago; special items $280 million; capex approximately $1.6 billion in the quarter, in line with full-year guidance; free cash flow ex-special items negative $765 million, hit by a delay in a $400 million tax refund now expected in 2026. North America enterprise revenue 'increased slightly driven by continued strength in IP'; wholesale declined approximately 7.8%. Lumen introduced a new strategic vs legacy reporting view this quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.041 billion (declined 8.7%); Business segment $2.425 billion (declined 8.8%); Mass Markets $616 million (declined 7.9%); adjusted EBITDA $767 million (25.2% margin); free cash flow negative $765 million; capex approximately $1.6 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: PCF (Private Connectivity Fabric) - 'a banner performance in PCF sales in the fourth quarter'. Lumen inked 'roughly $2.5 billion of new PCF deals' in Q4 and signed 'almost $4.5 billion in new PCF deals' over the past twelve months, taking total signed deals to 'nearly $13 billion with more deals in the pipeline' (versus the first $5.5 billion announced just over eighteen months earlier with a goal of $12 billion over time). PCF revenue recognized was roughly 41 million in Q4 and $116 million for FY2025 - 'it's starting to scale and ramp now' and 'we are either on or ahead of delivery schedule at this point with all of our customers'. Deal economics: the new deals are done 'on existing network conduit, so they don't have new routes', so the economic profile matches the earlier deals; guidance has been that '90% of the cash is received upfront for the bills' and 10% as the fiber is lit, with revenue recognized only when the fiber is lit. Timing: 'It's gonna take three years for those for those routes to get built at scale'; the $13 billion builds 'go all the way out through 2031', and the exit-2028 revenue ranges given earlier 'are not inclusive of what we just sold in Q4 because those bills won't be completed until after 2028'. Working capital 'will definitely be positive' with PCF inflows on the balance sheet and outflows in capex.
quarterly_data.figure: roughly $2.5 billion of new PCF deals in Q4; almost $4.5 billion signed over twelve months; nearly $13 billion total signed; PCF revenue roughly 41 million (Q4) and $116 million (FY2025)

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: AI BACKBONE BUILD. CEO Johnson: Lumen 'successfully reached our 2025 goal of implementing 17 million intercity fiber miles', and the Q4 PCF deals 'will raise our total network expansion to a whopping 58 million fiber miles in 2031'. Three major network upgrades: 'Building 400 gig rapid route waves across 36 routes, with more on the way, enabling 400 gig services for data centers across key markets, and focusing on metro expansion' to connect the most needed routes, data centers and cities. The 58 million fiber miles serve hyperscalers 'connecting their data centers' (the supply side), enterprise utilization (the demand side) and spare capacity - in 2031 Lumen expects to have more available for growth than when the journey started in 2022. Lumen positions its network on three AI metrics: 'Fastest time to first token, GPU idle time, and interconnect latency', and says that 'as data centers begin to decentralize to accommodate energy supply constraints, our vast network provides valuable proximity'.
quarterly_data.figure: 17 million intercity fiber miles (2025 goal reached); 58 million fiber miles in 2031; 400 gig rapid route waves across 36 routes

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: HYPERSCALER DEMAND AND BUILD SPEED. Asked whether customers could pause builds over bubble concerns, management said: 'Hyperscalers are not talking about a bubble. They are talking about they don't have enough fast enough', and 'many of our contracts have performance bonuses in them for us to go faster'. Also: 'the general feeling in the market is how fast can you go?' Lumen avoids construction delays through scale across the supply chain ('our contracts are very favorable and terms of first off the line priority status') and workforce, and on fiber supply management said 'we've got a very special relationship with Corning' and 'we are doing very well in terms of access to fiber' (the CEO also said Lumen 'expanded our partnership with Corning, ensuring we have priority access to the newest state-of-the-art fiber technology'), and because many deals are 'two existing data center areas where our network has proximity' - overbuilding rather than building for the first time. A large deal with an unnamed cloud company, the first time Lumen had worked with it, went so fast that its head of operations called to say they had 'never experienced this kind of speed before' with a telco. Per the CEO, 'the largest tech companies are choosing Lumen to help construct the supply side of the AI economy'.

FY2026 outlook (point-in-time, given on the day after the AT&T close and including its impact): adjusted EBITDA $3.1 billion to $3.3 billion, expected to 'inflect a growth in 2026'; pro forma economics for the divested fiber to the home business were to be released in an 8-K the next day. Guidance assumes organic business revenue declines roughly 75 basis points better than 2025 and excludes roughly $400 million of transformation costs. Total capex $3.2 billion to $3.4 billion, of which capex tied to the nearly $13 billion of PCF deals is approximately $1 billion ('those deals are prefunded'); CFO: 'outside of PCF, we're at about a $2 billion business', a capex intensity 'roughly half of where we were last year'. Free cash flow $1.2 billion to $1.4 billion; net cash interest $650 million to $750 million; cash taxes an inflow of 350 to $450 million. Cost-out target $700 million run rate exiting 2026, toward $1 billion by year-end 2027. The five-year model to be shown at the February 25 Investor Day is 'fully funded' with no need to borrow.
quarterly_data.figure: adjusted EBITDA $3.1 billion to $3.3 billion; capex $3.2 billion to $3.4 billion (PCF approximately $1 billion); free cash flow $1.2 billion to $1.4 billion; net cash interest $650 million to $750 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiber-to-the-home exit closed: the sale of the fiber to the home business to AT&T for $5.75 billion closed February 2 (the day before the call). Net proceeds and cash on hand paid down the full $4.8 billion of super priority bonds (second lien debt was also paid off in the prior month); total debt is now under $13 billion, leverage 3.8 times trailing twelve months adjusted EBITDA, and annual interest expense is down roughly $500 million versus 2025 levels. CEO: the divestiture 'reduces our annual CapEx by over $1 billion' as Lumen stops fiber to the home builds and focuses capital on 'building a digital network services company' serving enterprises as 'the trusted network for AI'. Seven debt refinancings in 2025 totaled over $11 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: fiber to the home business sold to AT&T for $5.75 billion; $4.8 billion super priority bonds paid down; debt under $13 billion; leverage 3.8 times; annual CapEx reduced by over $1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CALL-ONLY: MIX SHIFT AND DIGITAL/NaaS ADOPTION. 52% of North American enterprise revenue now comes from growth products, up from the mid 40% range in 2024, supporting the target of business revenue growth in 2028 and total revenue growth in 2029; the new 'strategic' bucket (which absorbed digitally delivered products such as Ethernet on demand and VPN on demand, and dropped declining lower-capacity connectivity lines) is expected to keep growing from 52%. NaaS: active customers grew by 29% quarter over quarter and services sold grew 26%; 900 off-net ports were announced as sold in October; NaaS churn rates are 'dramatically less than what we see on traditional sales'. Strength in IP; 'across all connectivity solutions there's demand right now'. LumenConnect ecosystem: 16 connected ecosystem partnerships signed, yielding more than 180 potential sales opportunities; announcements include a gated preview of AWS Interconnect and Lumen Defender with Microsoft Sentinel. Run rate cost savings exited 2025 at over $400 million.
quarterly_data.figure: 52% of North American enterprise revenue from growth products (up from the mid 40% range in 2024); NaaS active customers grew by 29%, services sold grew 26%; 16 connected ecosystem partnerships; over $400 million in run rate savings
